v1.2.1: Fix XHTTP inbound creation and form-urlencoded JSON corruption

Two bugs prevented XHTTP from working:

1. Port conflict: Both Reality TCP and XHTTP tried to bind port 443 in
   standalone mode. Fixed by giving XHTTP a dedicated port (xhttp_port).

2. Silent JSON corruption: Ansible's uri module with body_format
   form-urlencoded silently corrupts inline JSON values — the 3x-ui API
   returns success but stores only the first key name instead of the full
   JSON object. Fixed by switching all inbound API calls to body_format
   json with jinja2_native=True for proper type handling.

Add apt fallback for Ansible installation

The install_ansible() function tried apt-get but not apt. On some
minimal Linux environments (e.g. WSL), apt-get may not be configured
while apt works. Add apt as a fallback after apt-get.

Retry Ansible collection install up to 3 times

ansible-galaxy collection install can fail with network timeouts on
flaky connections. Retry up to 3 times with a short delay between
attempts before failing.

Suggest uninstall + retry on inbound creation failures

When 3x-ui API rejects an inbound (e.g. port conflict from corrupted
DB), the error now tells users to run 'meridian uninstall' and retry,
and links to GitHub issues if the problem persists.

Add Xray health check after inbound creation

After all inbounds are configured, verify that Xray core is actually
running inside the container. If xray crashed (e.g. from corrupted
config), the panel stays responsive but no traffic flows — this was
a silent failure that left users confused. Now fails early with
container logs and a suggestion to uninstall + retry.

Fix CLI server install for non-root users

Direct scp to /usr/local/bin/ fails for non-root users. Fall back to
scp to /tmp then sudo mv, which works when the user has sudo access
(which they do — ansible_become: true is set for non-root).

Don't downgrade on auto-update when running a dev version

When testing a local dev build with a higher version than published,
auto-update would "downgrade" to the older published version. Now
compares semver numerically and skips update if local is already
newer than remote.

Replace eval with printf -v in prompt() to prevent code injection

eval "$varname=\$value" could execute arbitrary code if terminal
input contained shell metacharacters. printf -v safely assigns to
a named variable without eval.

Add SHA256 checksum verification to auto-update

CD workflow now generates SHA256SUMS alongside CLI files on GitHub
Pages. The auto-update verifies the downloaded script's checksum
before writing to disk. If checksums are unavailable (first deploy),
update proceeds without verification. Cross-platform: uses sha256sum
on Linux, shasum -a 256 on macOS.

Fix PATH for non-interactive SSH shells

Prepend PATH export before .bashrc interactivity guard instead of
appending after it. Debian/Ubuntu .bashrc has `case $- in *i*) ;;
*) return;; esac` near the top — anything appended after it is
unreachable for `ssh host 'meridian ...'`. Use marker-based
idempotency check (not dir string match) to avoid false positives
from uv's env sourcing.

Fix non-root on-server execution: use local mode with sudo

Instead of hard-failing when a non-root user runs meridian on the
server, activate local mode with needs_sudo=True. Commands run via
`sudo bash -c '...'`, credentials are copied via `sudo -n cat`.
This lets `meridian scan`, `check`, `client list` etc. work without
requiring `sudo meridian` prefix.

Harden nginx against censor probing: default 403/404, no IP-mode redirect

the previous default — 444 (silent close after TLS handshake) — as 9/10

connection. Changed default to 403 on root + 404 on other paths, which
matches genuine nginx with an empty docroot (rated 3-4/10, 40-60%
false-positive cost for censors).

redirecting to HTTPS that returns 403 is a contradiction signal. Port 80

timeout must account for handshake overhead. 5s was too tight for
trivial commands like chmod, test -f, which, mkdir on slow or congested
links. Longer timeouts (60s+) for apt/docker/acme.sh are unchanged.

- Docker compose up, acme.sh install: 120s (was 60s)

Fix SSH drop-in priority: 99-meridian.conf → 00-meridian.conf

OpenSSH uses "first value wins" for sshd_config.d drop-ins. The 99-
prefix meant cloud-init's 01- or 50-cloud-init.conf would override
Meridian's PasswordAuthentication setting, causing the sshd -T check
to fail on every fresh Ubuntu cloud image.

00- prefix ensures Meridian's hardening loads first. On redeploy,
the old 99-meridian.conf is removed to avoid duplicate drop-ins.

Fix SCP directory copy broken on OpenSSH ≥ 9.0

OpenSSH 9.0+ defaults to SFTP protocol for scp, which changes how
directory copies work: scp -r dir/ host:/dest/ copies the directory
itself as a subdirectory instead of its contents. This put credentials
at /etc/meridian/<ip>/proxy.yml instead of /etc/meridian/proxy.yml,
causing relay remove to silently fail and subsequent deploys to read
stale data.

Replace directory-level scp -r with file-by-file scp, which behaves
identically across all OpenSSH versions.
